title: Sleeper Car to Nowhere in Particular
script: Narrator: [reflective] Sleeper compartments have a strange intimacy to them, four strangers folded into a space barely large enough for their luggage, let alone their inhibitions.
Narrator: [observant] The man in the upper bunk had brought a battered chess set, insisting almost immediately that we play before either of us had said much else.
Narrator: [wry] I lost within eleven moves, a fact he seemed determined to mention at every subsequent stop the train made that night.
Narrator: [thoughtful] There's something disarming about sharing a small space with people you'll never see again, a kind of freedom in the sheer impermanence of it.
Narrator: [honest] I told him things I hadn't told close friends, not because he was owed them, but because the conversation had nowhere permanent to land.
Narrator: [reflective] He mentioned, almost in passing, that he'd been laid off that week and was travelling simply because the ticket was already booked.
Narrator: [observant] Neither of us made much of the confession; it sat between us the way ordinary weather might, acknowledged, then quietly set aside.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I've noticed this pattern on every long train journey since, a peculiar honesty that daylight and permanence usually discourage entirely.
Narrator: [reflective] Perhaps it's the darkness outside the window, or the shared discomfort of narrow bunks, that dissolves the usual caution.
Narrator: [honest] By morning, we'd exchanged almost nothing practical, no numbers, no addresses, just a rematch he insisted on winning properly this time.
Narrator: [wry] He won, decisively, and seemed considerably more satisfied by that than by anything either of us had confessed the night before.
Narrator: [thoughtful] We parted at a platform neither of us had planned to visit, and I've thought about him more than most people I've actually kept in touch with.
Narrator: [reflective] There's a particular kind of relationship, I've decided, that only exists because it was never meant to last beyond one single journey.
Narrator: [with a small smile] I still don't know his surname, only that he plays a patient, slightly merciless game of chess.
Narrator: [reflective] Some encounters aren't meant to continue; they're meant to be entirely themselves, briefly, and then, quite deliberately, over.

quiz.question: What does the man in the upper bunk insist on doing almost immediately?
options: Sharing his food
Playing a game of chess before they had said much else
Reading a book aloud
Sleeping right away
quiz.explanation: He insists on playing chess with the narrator almost as soon as the journey begins.

quiz.question: Why does the narrator find herself confiding in a stranger?
options: He was a trained counselor
The conversation had nowhere permanent to land, unlike with close friends
She was forced to by the train staff
She had known him for years already
quiz.explanation: She explains she shared things with him precisely because the exchange had no lasting consequences.

quiz.question: What does the man reveal about his week before the trip?
options: He had just gotten married
He had been laid off and was travelling because the ticket was already booked
He was moving permanently abroad
He had won a large sum of money
quiz.explanation: He mentions almost in passing that he'd lost his job and was travelling only because the ticket was pre-booked.

quiz.question: What happens with the chess rematch by morning?
options: The narrator wins this time
He wins decisively and seems more satisfied by that than by the night's confessions
They never finish the game
They both agree to a draw
quiz.explanation: He wins the rematch decisively and appears more pleased by that than by anything confessed the night before.

quiz.question: What is the narrator's final reflection on this kind of encounter?
options: She regrets not exchanging contact information
Some encounters are meant to be entirely themselves briefly, then deliberately over
She plans to find him again someday
Train journeys are generally unpleasant
quiz.explanation: She concludes that some relationships exist only to be brief and complete in themselves, never meant to continue.
